newsitem.title: ROMANIA: RADIO ROMANIA AFTERNOON HEADLINES AT 4 PM.
newsitem.headline: RADIO ROMANIA AFTERNOON HEADLINES AT 4 PM.

text.p: * Ceremonies marking seven years since the bloody Romanian revolution which toppled former dictator Nicolae Ceausescu include a day of mourning in the western city of Timisoara to honour the numerous deaths on December 17, 1989.
* The Chamber of Deputies started debate on a road traffic bill which is expected to settle the question of pollution by outdated Romanian-made trucks and lorries.

* A delegation of the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development met Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea to present a report of the bank's support so far in financing Romania's privatisation and infrastructure projects.

* The delegation, led by the EBRD's director for Eastern Europe, Joshua Tanaka, met President Emil Constantinescu to examine the implications of Romania's bid to join the European Union as well as the economic tasks awaiting the country.
The EBRD agreed to set up a system of regular consultations with the presidency on vital issues for Romania's economy.
* Reform Minister Ulm Spineanu held a news conference to present his plans on swift privatisation and structural reform to make Romanian industry competitive.

* The miners confederation from the coal region of the Jiu Valley announced on Tuesday that unions would not demand wage rises until August 1997 provided that the system of indexations and state subsidies for the sector were maintained.
* The new Health Minister, Iosif Dragulescu, told a news conference he wanted four percent of the country's gross domestic product devoted to the ministry budget in 1997.
* Party of Social Democracy leader Adrian Nastase slammed the government for replacing the general manager of the national television, saying the measure breached the constitution.
